title: Absalom Lament
program_note:
Absalom Lament and Jerusalem Hallelujah are, together, the final two numbers of the Max Helfman Composers Group’s oratorio on the life of the biblical King David, called David’s Quilt.  In Absalom Lament we hear David mourning the death of his rebellious son Absalom, consoled by the sound of the harp (David’s instrument).  Escaping the spiral of guilt and sorrow he shifts his thoughts to Solomon, his son who would succeed him on the throne; toward the end of this more penitential portion of the number, the choir joins him to sing “Oh Lord, open my lips, and let my mouth sing your praise/ With music our souls he equips, so to heaven a song we’ll raise.” This propels them into Jerusalem Hallelujah, the closing number, a combination of Psalms 122 and 147 that together praises God and Jerusalem, the city that the Davidic dynasty would build.

Absalom Lament is approximately 6 minutes and Jerusalem Hallelujah is approximately 4 minutes in duration.

David S. Lefkowitz
8 August, 2017
Los Angeles, CA
